value: The durability of a stone — committed AND pushed — becomes a lane on the PROVED exit gate, composing repo_truth(), so a stone cannot close over work that exists only on this laptop.

One, and it is yours because it is a cost you bear, not a fact anyone can measure: SHOULD THE LANE REFUSE WHEN THE PUSH TARGET IS UNREACHABLE? A network outage would turn into a blocked voyage. My read is refuse anyway — a gate that stands down when the network is bad stands down exactly when the work is least durable, and GitHub here is hosting-only with no CI, so an outage has never blocked anything and the cost is a pause, not a broken build. But it is your laptop and your patience, so if you would rather it degrade to a loud journaled warning on an unreachable remote, say so and that is what it does. Everything else on this ticket is settled by measurement or by an existing charter.

ANSWERED FROM THE CORPUS (CC, 2026-09-09): refuse anyway. The lane never dials — measured: repo_truth has 0 fetch hits, the gate reads local git plumbing (rev-parse, status, the remote-tracking ref) and never the network — so an outage cannot block a voyage at this lane; the only thing it can do is read 'not pushed' truthfully, which is the finding. GitHub is hosting-only (no CI), so 'unreachable remote' is a pause to push, not a broken build. Standing unless Akien says degrade.
